faults.fault_text: The harness leaves turned_own_test out of P4.2 and P4.3 with the reason 'no arms document affords it', where the instrument's own table says in the same file that this field is 'NOT RECORDED by the corpus: unknown, and read ... it is not excluded from P4.2 and P4.3, because an exclusion needs evidence'. The table uses one shape - an empty affords list - for two different things: test_patches, which coverage.md records as afforded by nothing, and turned_own_test, which the corpus does not record either way. agreement.py reads only the list (afforded = bool(aff[name]) when the name is in the table), so both come out False. The read-me states the right rule and the wrong test for it: 'A field the table does not name is read, not excluded - found nowhere means unknown'; turned_own_test IS named, so the rule never reaches it. This is the skill's own 'Found nowhere means unknown' being written down and then not obeyed, and it is a seam neither fixer would take: A4 reported it in its dropped list and did not fix it because no fault named it and I had verified fault 18 on the table as it stands.

faults.forced_fix: One of the two moves, and one file changes. Either agreement.py reads the row's status (or its basis) and treats a row whose affords list is empty because the corpus does not record the field as a field the table does not name - read, not excluded - or affordance.json stops naming such a field at all, so the read-me's existing rule reaches it.
